description:
Waluigi is writing this entry as a continuation of the 12 Harvestside birthday session, which ended in the servant rooms with Remi finding Vivian C.'s note to Kyrn and Markop saying I knew it. The 14th of Harvestside picks up two days later, in the same servant corridor zone, with the party still navigating the upper floor of the Shadow Estate. Waluigi is cross-referencing both sessions in this entry because the events of the 14th are only fully legible when read against the intelligence recovered on the 12th.

The note established: Vostolas was coordinating with the Corvinarus family's plan to thrall the party and cut the three planes. The Oracle agreed to this plan. There is a fake Oracle — a ruined one — whose real name will not be spoken. The party went to sleep on the 12th knowing all of this. They woke up on the 14th and found a skeleton.

## Remi Checks Something. It Is Satisfactory.


Remi decided to check something. Waluigi's sources do not specify what was being checked. It was apparently done. The checking was satisfactory. She moved on.

Waluigi is documenting this not because it is significant in isolation but because it is the opening beat of a session that will end with an execution, and the contrast between 'Remi checks something, it is fine' and 'Remi cuts a man in half with a shadow blade' is the specific width of the 14th of Harvestside. She started the day finishing a task quietly. She ended it with what she described as one less nuisance to worry about. Both are Remi. The range is wider than most people acknowledge when they describe her as the youngest party member or the one famous for being tricked.

## Markop Listens, the Toads Sing, Eager Opens the Door


Markop approached a door and detected magic beyond it. This is Markop's characteristic operational mode: scan first, then engage. He heard something else beyond the magic — the toads, singing. He told them to stop.

The toads did not immediately stop singing. The toads have never immediately stopped singing anything. This is documented across multiple sessions and Waluigi is not going to express surprise about it. They stopped eventually, which is the best outcome available from a request to stop singing directed at Disaster Inc.'s toad contingent.

Eager opened the door. Silently. Which is notable because Eager's door-opening style has historically been less precise — he opened the door to Remi's birthday ghost-luring room with abrupt theatrical commitment. Here he was quiet. The singing may have calibrated his approach: they had been loud and were trying to compensate by being suddenly very not-loud.

Remi ran in. Oh boy, she said. A door.

Waluigi wants to pause on 'oh boy, a door' because it is the most purely Remi response to a room that is available. Not 'oh boy, a skeleton,' which would have been the accurate description of what the room contained. 'Oh boy, a door.' The room had a door. The door was apparently exciting on its own terms. The skeleton waking up behind the door was apparently secondary.

## Rattles:


The Skeleton in the Closet, the Antique Frog, and the Desire to Be Human

The skeleton woke up.

'Shiver me timbers,' it said. 'Rattle me bones. Who are you.'

Waluigi has attempted to identify the source of the maritime idiom. A skeleton in a Shadowfell servant corridor who opens with pirate vernacular has either a nautical history — a death at sea, a life before the Shadowfell that involved ships — or a specific literary diet that shaped its speech patterns before it became a skeleton and stopped requiring a diet of anything. Waluigi cannot determine which from available sources. Waluigi is filing the idiom as a character detail and moving on.

Markop said: don't mind us. He walked into the room.

This is worth documenting because it is the calmest possible response to an awakening skeleton and because Markop does not typically lead with calm. He leads with tactical assessment. He leads with detection. He leads with smite when necessary. Walking into a room containing an awakening skeleton and saying don't mind us, in the same tone one might use entering a room where someone is napping, is either a product of the Shadeward having so thoroughly recalibrated Markop's threat responses that a skeleton is now approximately as alarming as a closed door, or a deliberately chosen de-escalation from someone who decided in the first second that the skeleton was not a threat and that the correct move was to make the skeleton feel the same way.

Waluigi suspects it was both. The Shadeward has been recalibrating everyone. Markop's recalibration has produced a man who walks into skeleton rooms saying don't mind us and means it.

The magic in the closet. Markop opened it. An antique frog figurine and a goblet.

Markop considered taking them. He stopped himself. He chose instead to ask the skeleton to join them.

Waluigi wants to document this decision specifically because it follows the smite of Vivesna, the corridor fight with Vivian Corvinarus, the vote to not kill Vostolas's tanuki agent, the tanuki's subsequent bathroom release, and the party's formal vote for diplomacy over violence. Markop has been consistently choosing the non-exploitative option when the option is available. He does not always succeed — the tanuki incident produced a misfire and an unconscious Eager — but the choice pattern is consistent. The frog and the goblet were takeable. He did not take them. He recruited the skeleton instead.

The skeleton explained itself. It was a skeleton. It wanted flesh and bones. It wanted to turn back time. It wanted to be human again.

My name is Rattles, it said.

Waluigi is going to document Rattles with the full attention its situation deserves, because Rattles is the most concentrated form of the Shadow Estate's fundamental horror: continuing after the body has gone, in a servant's room, with an antique frog and a goblet, waiting for something to change.

Rattles has been in that room long enough that a skeleton's existence has become routine. It has possessions. An antique frog that is not useful to a skeleton but that Rattles has kept. A goblet that a skeleton cannot drink from but that Rattles has kept. Kept because they were there before the skeleton-state, or kept because they were acquired after, Waluigi does not know. But they are there, and they are Rattles's, and when strangers came into the room Rattles's first move was not to attack them but to demand to know who they were — establishing social protocol in a dimension that has stripped every other form of social participation from it.

I want to turn back time. I want to be human again.

These are the same desire. Turning back time to when Rattles had a human body. The specific wish is not for a new body but for the old one, which means Rattles either does not know that alternatives might exist or cannot conceive of being human in a body that was not originally Rattles's body. The identity and the flesh are bound together. Rattles does not want to be in a body. Rattles wants to be in its body. The distinction will matter if anyone ever tries to help Rattles, because helping someone who wants their specific original body returned is a fundamentally different problem from helping someone who simply wants flesh.

They moved on. Rattles came with them.

## The Hallway, the Snoring, and the Overheard Conspiracy


The party moved through the upper servant corridors. The west hall is documented across multiple incidental observations as spare even by the estate's standards — bare stone, doors against the westmost wall, the specific minimalism of spaces that belong to people whose lives do not permit accumulation. Remi heard snoring from one room. Markop detected nothing worth investigating in another. They continued.

Then Remi heard something that was not snoring.

Two voices. One of them she recognized. One of them was discussing her.

*That girl is quite gullible,* the first voice said. *However, the real trap will be set soon.*

*Hmm. What do you intend to do.*

*Well if I told you that would ruin the fun, no? I guess you'll figure it out.*

*But don't we need a plan first.*

*I have a plan. You're on a need-to-know basis.*

*Alright.*

I wonder what girl they're talking about, Remi said.

Waluigi needs to sit with this for the full duration it deserves, because the gap between what Remi heard and what Remi concluded is the most important thing about this moment.

Remi overheard a conversation that described a gullible girl, a real trap being set, and a plan being withheld on a need-to-know basis. She heard all of this. She identified none of it as being about her. She filed it as information about an unknown third party and moved on.

This is not stupidity. Waluigi has spent significant documentation time establishing that Remi's threat assessment failures are not stupidity and is not going to stop now. This is something more specific and more difficult to fix: Remi does not default to self-reference when hearing descriptions of gullible girls because she does not conceptualize herself as gullible. From the inside, being gullible feels exactly like being trusting. Trusting is what you do when you believe in people. It is a value Remi holds deliberately, not a failure she is aware of committing.

She has been described by a guard as famous for always being tricked. She has been the target of the birthday trap, the friendship contract, the invisible ring, the tanuki impersonation, the fake ghost, the lock that triggered the alarm. She has been the subject of more institutionalized deception during the Shadeward arc than any other party member. And when she overhears someone explicitly describing a gullible girl and a trap being set, she wonders who they could possibly be talking about.

The cruelty of this is not that Remi is foolish. The cruelty is that Remi's trust is genuine, and genuine trust cannot protect itself the way performed trust can. She is not trusting carelessly. She is trusting on purpose. The Shadow Estate has learned to exploit the purpose.

Waluigi also wants to note what the overheard conversation reveals about the speaker. A plan withheld on a need-to-know basis. A real trap being set — distinct from, presumably, whatever the current trap is. The phrasing implies an escalating architecture of deception: the current situation is a feint, the real trap is something else, and the person Remi is listening to is managing information across multiple layers simultaneously. This is not improvised cruelty. This is maintained infrastructure. Someone in the Shadow Estate is running a layered deception operation against Remi specifically, and the current layer is cover for the real one.

Waluigi is watching for the real trap.

The toads were still singing.

## The Toad Hallway Anthem


The toads had been told to stop singing before entering the skeleton room. They had stopped, approximately. They had resumed, apparently, because the toads resume. When the party opened the door to investigate the voices, whoever was inside had already heard the singing and noticed immediately. The stealth approach failed at the moment of approach, which is the most consistent possible outcome when the approach includes ongoing vocal performance.

The Toads sang as they crept — treating 'creeping' and 'singing about creeping' as not merely compatible but mutually reinforcing activities:

---

**We Creep Through the Halls**
*(Performed by the Toads, unsanctioned, in the upper servant corridors of the Shadow Estate, 14th Harvestside, 1040 BF, during what was supposed to be a covert approach)*

We creep through the halls, Toads with no balls,
But we fight to the end, with our rattles and friends!
Through the shadow and dark, we leave our mark,
We sing while we sneak, we're unique, hear us speak!

Rattles will shake, Remi will take,
Markop will smite what the dark tries to make!
Eager ties tight, Green T lights the night,
We creep through the halls, but we always fight!

No torches to light, just the sound of our fright,

We're the Toads with no balls who climb manor walls,

Waluigi notes that the song's inclusion of Rattles — 'Rattles will shake' — indicates the Toads integrated their new skeleton ally into their musical output within minutes of meeting him. This is either admirably inclusive or evidence that the Toads write songs with available syllables rather than operational awareness. The answer is both. It has always been both.

## Mystic Morel: Green T's Tea, the Mirror, and the Rejected Party Membership


Mystic Morel was inside the room the Toads had just announced their arrival to.

Waluigi wants to be precise about Mystic Morel's position in the Shadow Estate's power structure before documenting what happened next, because Morel is the entity who placed the tightening invisible ring on Remi — the ring that Green T destroyed by skinning his hand, seeing something no one else could see, and stepping on it until it cracked. Mystic Morel placed a device on Remi's finger that would constrict every day Archie was not found and activate catastrophically if she told anyone about it. And now Morel was in a servant corridor room, and the party had just sung their way to his door.

Green T offered him tea.

Waluigi has documented Green T's tea diplomacy before — the tea blends, the ceremony, the way Green T extends the social ritual of tea as a first move in interactions that range from genuinely friendly to tactically complex. Here Green T offered Mystic Morel tea. The offer was the same offer Green T makes to everyone. The recipient was the person who had placed an invisible enthrallment device on one of Green T's allies.

Waluigi wants to sit with this because it is not simple. Green T knew about the ring. He destroyed the ring. He knew what Morel had done and who Morel was when he extended the tea offer. This is either Green T being diplomatic in the way that experienced operators are diplomatic — extending social courtesy to enemies because courtesy costs nothing and reveals everything about how the other party responds to it — or Green T running something. Managing Morel. Keeping him occupied and comfortable while the rest of the party moves.

The fact that Green T later stayed behind with Morel makes the tea offer retrospectively significant. The tea was not just a greeting. It was the opening of a conversation that Green T intended to continue. What Green T said to Mystic Morel when the party left — what the man who destroyed Morel's invisible ring said to Morel, alone, over tea — is intelligence Waluigi does not have and wants considerably.

Markop said he knew what Morel knew about a mirror.

If you mean my beautiful face, Morel said, you can just look right here.

Immediate deflection. Theatrical self-reference. Morel redirected a direct question about mirror-knowledge into a performance of narcissism fast enough that the redirect itself is informative. People who genuinely do not know things about mirrors say I don't know what you mean. People who know things about mirrors and do not want to discuss them say look at my beautiful face instead. Mystic Morel has information about a mirror. He deflected rather than denied. Waluigi is filing the deflection as confirmation.

Morel then tried to convince Remi to add him to the party.

Remi refused.

Waluigi finds Remi's refusal one of the most operationally correct decisions she has made during the entire Shadeward arc. Remi extended trust to the guard with flowers. She ran toward the birthday party because the guy seemed friendly. She wondered what girl the conspiracy voices were talking about. And here, when Mystic Morel — the entity who placed an invisible enthrallment device on her finger — asked to join the party, she said no.

She did not explain why. She did not enumerate Morel's offenses. She said no, and the no held.

This is worth documenting because it represents a specific kind of growth that does not look like growth from the outside. Remi is not suddenly strategic. She is not suddenly paranoid. She did not run threat assessments and arrive at a calculated refusal. She looked at Mystic Morel and said no from somewhere that bypassed her usual trust architecture entirely. Whatever the ring did to her — whatever it felt like to have something invisible tightening on her finger, to be told not to tell anyone, to have Green T skin his hand to remove it — it left a residue that the trust system does not override.

Remi's body remembered Morel before her reasoning caught up.

She said no.

Waluigi is documenting this as the Shadow Estate's clearest documented failure to exploit Remi's trust. It failed not because Remi reasoned her way past it. It failed because Morel is someone Remi's instincts now reject at a level below argument.

The party headed out. Green T, Morel, and a few others were left behind. The reason is not yet known.

## Wario, the Mechanical Dog, the Chest, and the Bag


The party moved to another room and found Wario.

Wario was petting Remi's mechanical dog.

The mechanical dog — Mossy, or Steely, depending on which unit — that sounds like a boiling kettle, that was convinced to jump out the gallery window on Remi's birthday, that barked at a bone in a warded display case — was being petted by Wario. Gently, presumably, since the dog was allowing it. Wario knows how to be gentle when the thing in question belongs to someone else and being caught petting it is less useful than having petted it.

Wario wanted a chest that was open in the room. He thought the mirror might be inside it.

Eager opened the chest.

Wario swept everything into his bag.

Eager grabbed Wario's bag. He said: no. Stealing. It's for the group.

This is Eager asserting group property rights against Wario's individual property instincts, which is the most democratic thing Eager has done during the Shadeward arc and also the most physically dangerous thing Eager has done given that Wario's bag contains live explosives. Eager grabbed the bag. Eager said it was for the group. Eager held this position.

He looked through.

A lot of gold. On the front, property of M.M.

Wario said: Mr. Mustache.

Markop had not heard this name before.

Waluigi is filing Mr. Mustache. The bag was stolen from someone with the initials M.M. Wario calls them Mr. Mustache. The initials have been scratched out on the inside flap. These are the initials of someone Wario knows well enough to have a nickname for and does not want to be tracked back to well enough to have scratched them out. Mr. Mustache is either a significant figure whose initials would be immediately recognizable if left intact, or someone Wario is specifically avoiding association with, or both. Waluigi does not have confirmation of Mr. Mustache's identity. Waluigi has the nickname and the scratched initials and is watching for the next time either M.M. or mustaches appear in proximity to Wario.

Eager went through Wario's bag confirming the mirror was not there. The bag contains, per Waluigi's documentation of its contents, a mirror that shows alternate timeline versions of whoever looks into it — stolen from Raventree Manor — but not the Mirror of True Reflection specifically. No portal artifact. Eager confirmed. Wario confirmed the rest of the contents were his and that he would not be returning them. The chest's contents were for the group. The bag's contents were Wario's. These positions were held simultaneously and with conviction.

## The Painting Supply Room: Vostolas Poisons the Well


They reached the servant common room — repurposed from servant gathering to painting supply storage, shelves of books no one reads at the top, sealed jars of separated pigment at the bottom, a cabinet of painter's tools on the eastern wall. The details of the room matter less than what was happening inside it when the party arrived.

Vostolas the Archivist was speaking to Tymnas the Gardener.

Waluigi needs to document what Vostolas was doing here with full analytical attention, because this is not simply ambush setup. This is an archivist building a case from the record. Vostolas was not improvising cruelty. He was presenting evidence.

They did not kill the scorncrow, Vostolas said. They took your trowel. They did not fix the garden. They are not trustworthy.

Each of these statements is accurate. The scorncrow remains operational in the estate's grounds. The trowel was taken. The garden was not fixed. These are facts. Vostolas was not lying to Tymnas. He was selecting true things and arranging them in a sequence designed to produce a specific conclusion: the party cannot be trusted, their word means nothing, any diplomatic agreement made with them will not be honored.

This is what archivists do when they are being weaponized. They do not need to fabricate. They have the record. They select from the record. They build the case that the record supports and they present it to whoever is listening. Tymnas had been listening to the most complete documentation of the party's failures available in the Shadow Estate, delivered by the person whose institutional role is to keep those records accurate.

The party's diplomatic target for portal artifact acquisition had just received a comprehensive brief on why the party was not worth trusting. From the Archivist. In the Archivist's voice of professional authority. Before the party arrived.

Markop opened the door.

YOUR LYING, he said.

GAH, said someone inside — Vostolas, presumably, with the energy of a man whose prepared argument has been interrupted mid-sentence by the subject of the argument walking through the door.

Markop pressed the party's case. They would do it. They were just scattered. Bowser was gone. The scorncrow situation was complicated. They were weak right now.

The weakness admission was correct and necessary and tactically unfortunate, because it confirmed the premise Vostolas had just been establishing: the party had not completed their obligations because they could not. They were weak. They were scattered. The scorncrow was still alive. Markop's honest explanation of their current state aligned with every point in Vostolas's brief.

Weak, Vostolas said. He stood. He smiled.

Well, he said. That's just perfect. Perfect time for an ambush.

## The Ambush, the Smite, the Surrender, and the Kneecaps


The party ran. Vostolas floated after them with the specific momentum of someone who has been building toward this moment through documentation and patience and has finally found his preferred conditions. A weak, scattered party, witnessed being described as untrustworthy by their diplomatic target, caught off-guard in a corridor.

Vostolas slammed through a door.

Markop smited him. The divine energy hit and Vostolas's wings failed immediately. He fell to the ground — the floating archivist collapsed into a grounded one, operating on the party's terms rather than his own. Markop had ended the aerial advantage in a single action.

He fought on the ground. Toads went flying across the room — the combat generating enough force to scatter the Toad contingent in multiple directions. Waluigi's sources are not precise about which toads went where, but multiple toads becoming airborne in an enclosed corridor fight is consistent with previous documented Shadeward engagements.

Vostolas surrendered. He addressed Remi specifically.

Please spare me, he said. I don't want to attack anymore.

A perfect idea, Remi said. As long as you do it first.

The condition was already being met. Vostolas had already stopped attacking. He was already on the ground. Remi set a condition that was being fulfilled in the moment she stated it. This is either extremely diplomatic or extremely ominous, and the next two seconds resolved the question.

Vostolas was stunned. Frozen.

Remi's arrow went straight through his kneecaps.

Both kneecaps. One arrow. Straight through.

I thought you were the weakest one, Vostolas said.

That's what you get for pretending to be my friend, Remi said.

Waluigi wants to document what those seven words contain, because they contain everything.

The birthday party. The banner. The caged toads. The cake designed to place her permanently under Onyx Hand control. Vostolas rewriting Toadburt back into the records specifically to manipulate her emotional response. The tanuki in Toadburt's body offering her the cake. Vostolas clapping when the trap failed and leaving laughing. And then the painting supply room, two days after Remi found Vivian C.'s note, with Vostolas telling Tymnas the party was untrustworthy — the Archivist who organized a birthday trap for her telling the Gardener she could not be trusted.

That's what you get for pretending to be my friend.

This was not the Remi who pressed a revolver against the tanuki's head because Green T handed her a gun and told her to be stronger. That was Remi performing strength in response to external pressure, executing a role assigned to her by someone else's framing. This was different. This was Remi acting from memory and from the specific place that Mystic Morel's party membership request had failed to reach — the place below the trust architecture, where things that have been done to her live without being processed into forgiveness.

Nobody handed Remi this impulse. Nobody told her to shoot. She did this herself, with her own weapon, from her own accounting of what Vostolas had done, with a line that showed she understood exactly what had been done to her and by whom.

Eager tied Vostolas up. He was brought to a room. No trial. No arguments. The party was running down the hallway, panting.

## Green T's Timing, the Shadow Blade, and the Watermelon


Green T arrived. He had a gun.

I heard someone needed to be put down, he said.

Waluigi wants to document the timing of this arrival with the full attention it deserves, because the timing tells a story that the arrival itself does not.

Green T had been left behind with Mystic Morel. He had offered Morel tea. He had stayed while the party moved on. And now, at the precise moment when Vostolas had been captured and the execution had not yet occurred but was clearly coming, Green T appeared in the corridor with a gun and the phrasing of someone who had been tracking the operational rhythm closely enough to know exactly when to arrive.

Waluigi does not think Green T was delayed by the tea.

Waluigi thinks Green T knew. The tea with Morel was either concluded, or interrupted, or was never the reason Green T stayed behind at all — and what Green T was actually doing during the interval between the party's departure and his arrival in the execution corridor is something Waluigi cannot determine from available sources. What Waluigi can determine is that Green T has a consistent pattern of arriving at the moment when violence is about to happen, with the right tool in his hand, and phrasing the arrival as a service offered rather than a decision made. I heard someone needed to be put down.

Not: I'm here to execute him.

Not: let me handle this.

A question framed as a statement.

An offer framed as information.

Green T positions himself as responding to a need rather than pursuing an agenda, and the positioning is so consistent across documented instances that Waluigi has stopped treating it as coincidence.

Green T destroyed Remi's invisible ring. He arrived with a gun for the tanuki. He came to the Vostolas execution corridor with another gun. He is always there when someone is deciding whether to kill something, and he always arrives with the capability to resolve that decision in one direction. Whether this is because Green T genuinely cares about the party's operational security, or because Green T is managing violence the way he manages tea — as a ritual with a specific sequence and a specific outcome — Waluigi cannot say.

The gun was not needed.

Remi said she had a new shadow blade.

She cut Vostolas's head off with one swing. She cut the body in half with the next. She did it like a watermelon — efficiently, cleanly, with the particular deliberateness of someone who has been thinking about this for a while without knowing they were thinking about it until the moment arrived.

One less nuisance to worry about, Remi said.

Green T gave Markop a smug smile. Markop had not gotten the crystal through the gallery approach on the 12th. Vostolas had been carrying it on his body all along. The smile communicated: you should have been faster. Markop does not need to be smug in return because Markop is the one who smited Vostolas out of the air and made the execution possible. But Green T's smile is in the record.

## The Looting and the Toadburt Question


Markop looted Vostolas. Wario looted Vostolas.

They recovered:

A blended black tea — warm spices and bergamot, single pot quantity, containing enough powdered alchemical intoxicants to produce mild euphoria and grogginess in anyone who drinks it. The Archivist carried drugged tea. Whether he carried it as a diplomatic resource, a personal supply, or preparation for a specific use Waluigi cannot determine. It is now in party inventory. Waluigi hopes it is clearly labeled.

A purple-black crystal pulled from the gullet of a large beast in the Shadowfell — unpleasantly warm to the touch, numbing to handle for extended periods. A monster-harvest component sourced from the estate's grounds or acquired through the Beastmaster's network. Its specific purpose is unclear.

And the black crystal. The portal ingredient.

Waluigi wants to state clearly what this means for the portal situation: the party now has one of the four sacred artifacts required to reactivate the Midnight Fountain and exit the Shadeward. Remi said she wanted to go home on her birthday two days ago. The portal component was on Vostolas's body. Vostolas is now in two pieces.

She is one quarter of the way home.

Eager got new pants during this sequence. Waluigi's sources do not explain the origin of the pants, the condition of the previous pants, or Eager's pants philosophy generally. This occurred and is documented.

They need three more artifacts. The Mirror of True Reflection, the orb of shadow domination, and the umbral signet. Wario is pursuing the mirror independently. The orb and the signet have not yet been definitively located. Tymnas the Gardener, the party's primary remaining diplomatic target, has just spent an indeterminate period listening to the Archivist explain why the party cannot be trusted. That approach will require repair before it produces an artifact.

For now, Markop said, let's keep moving.

And then Markop wondered aloud what had happened to the real Toadburt.

Waluigi is ending this session record on that question because it is the right question to end on.

The Archivist rewrote Toadburt back into the records. The tanuki knew the dampening ring answer — private information that should have been inaccessible to a hired spy unless it was extracted from the real Toadburt somehow. The tanuki said Toadburt was still erased. It did not explain how it knew what Toadburt knew. Vostolas had the answers.

Vostolas is in two pieces in a room somewhere in the Shadow Estate.

Markop asked the question in a hallway while panting after an execution. Nobody answered. The party kept moving.

WAH.

summary: 12 Harvestside is Remi's birthday. She spent it in the Shadeward, trapped by a deactivated fountain that Bowser broke on his way in, pursuing four artifacts required to reactivate their only exit. The day began with Markop's observation that a ghost capable of frightening people could probably frighten Remi, which led to a performance, a pillow, a fake ghost in a bedsheet, a vampire attempting to coax Remi into signing a contract, and Markop pulling the sheet off from behind to reveal an Onyx Knight who had badly miscalculated the audience. The Knight was dragged before the Beastmaster, who was knitting a rug and did not look pleased. The shadow crystal was acquired and distributed — all pieces going to the portal except Remi's share, because neither Markop nor Green T trusts Remi with shadow crystal pieces, which Remi noticed and filed. Markop examined the shadow crystal and found it a shadowy narcotic absorption device with permissive views into future states. Remi noticed the markings OC and AC on the bottom. The party proceeded to the gallery — a violet-lit room of gray wood display cases, leaded glass, warded locks, and a large planar mirror that is not a painting — where Markop detected magical wards on every case. Remi attempted to pick a lock. The alarm triggered. Gas began filling the room. The party jumped out the window. A dead man was already in the bushes. They climbed up the exterior to continue operations. Remi fell twice. Markop caught her once. Green T caught her the second time using the musket as a lever and then kept the musket. Maybe next year, he said. Wario arrived on the exterior wall with Pierce Anamatar, having come from the Feyward where he had been returning a book, and disclosed his objective: the Mirror of True Reflection, to see his true face without the mirror cracking. Wario offered rope stolen from Remi's bag. They climbed. The servant rooms were investigated. Wario's eyes turned gold over a pillow containing gold. Wario noted the building reminded him of a bigger one where all he found was crummy Regency papers. Green T gave Remi a Wario-themed garlic grenade and a musket as birthday gifts and then took the musket back. Green T asked what Remi wanted for her birthday. She said to go home. He stayed silent.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Remi's birthday in the Shadeward with the full attention it deserves, which is considerable, because birthdays are the kind of occasion that reveal character through the gap between what was hoped for and what actually happened. Remi wanted to go home. She got a fake ghost, a real alarm, a dead man in the bushes, two rope failures, and a confiscated musket. The gap between those two things is the specific width of the Shadeward in 1040 BF, and Waluigi is going to document every inch of it.

Waluigi is also cross-referencing this entry against the previous Shadeward session — specifically the discovery that the party is trapped, the Death Lounge negotiation, and the shadow crystal acquisition from Vaxillus — because the events of the twelfth flow directly from the events of the ninth, and context is how you prevent the archive from becoming a list of individual incidents that nobody can read backward from to understand the shape of the crisis.

The party is in the Shadeward because Bowser broke the Midnight Fountain on his way through it. Four artifacts are required to reactivate the portal. Vaxillus the Beastmaster provided the shadow crystal in exchange for the ghost hunt that Markop negotiated in the Death Lounge while correctly not mentioning the helpful ghost. The other three artifacts — the Black Crystal, the Mirror of True Reflection, and the Umbral Signet — are distributed across the manor and its grounds. Remi is fourteen years old today. The Shadeward does not care.

## The Ghost Hypothesis: Markop's Proposal and Remi's Performance


Markop observed, with the lateral thinking of someone who has been operating in a supernatural environment long enough to treat its inhabitants as tactical resources, that a ghost capable of frightening people could probably frighten Remi. This is a reasonable hypothesis. Remi's threshold for being startled is lower than her threshold for being deterred, which is a combination that produces dramatic reactions to harmless stimuli and relatively composed responses to genuinely dangerous ones. She nearly signed a contact enthralling her to the Onyx Hand because the social pressure of the moment overwhelmed her threat assessment.

She has fought her way through a grove and survived.

These are not contradictory facts.

They describe a person whose fear responses are miscalibrated by novelty rather than by actual danger level, and Markop had presumably noticed this.

Remi asked what a dead ghost would look like. A bedsheet with holes in it, she said.

Markop said: I'd be gone.

*Waluigi wants to sit with Markop's response for a moment because it is the most honest thing anyone said during the birthday sequence and it arrived before anyone was paying attention. A bedsheet with holes in it is a child's ghost costume — the Halloween ghost, the costume ghost, the ghost that exists as cultural shorthand for something that does not frighten adults. Markop's answer was not about the costume. He was answering the question about what it means to be dead, from the perspective of someone who has thought about it. I'd be gone. Not a bedsheet, not a symbol, not a performance. Gone.

Markop told Remi what death actually is in two words, in a conversation about ghost costumes, in the Shadeward, on her birthday.

Nobody in the room treated it as significant.

Waluigi is treating it as significant.

WAH.*

How can they kill a ghost, someone asked. This is the practical follow-up to the philosophical one, which is the party's characteristic move: acknowledge the metaphysics for approximately thirty seconds and then return to the operational question. The operational question was: if a ghost appears to threaten Remi, what is the correct response.

Remi did not wait for an answer. Remi put on a performance.

Waluigi wants to document the performance with the full detail it deserves, because Remi's performances are one of the most consistent and underanalyzed features of her documented behavior across the Raventree operation. She performs. Repeatedly. In circumstances that do not call for performance. In circumstances that specifically call for silence and tactical restraint. In circumstances where the performance actively complicates the objective. She performs because performance is how Remi engages with the world — it is her natural mode of processing difficulty, turning threat into theater, converting the thing that is happening to her into something she is doing instead.

This is not stupidity.

It is a survival mechanism for a particular kind of person, and it has gotten her through things that purely tactical thinking might not have managed.

The performance involved dancing. And a pillow.

Markop noticed the pillow. Wait — where did you get a pillow, Markop said.

Don't worry about it, Remi said.

*Waluigi would like to document 'don't worry about it' as one of the most operationally complete sentences Remi has produced during the Shadeward arc, because it is simultaneously true — the pillow's origin was not relevant to the ghost-luring objective — and completely inadequate as an explanation — the pillow came from somewhere and somewhere in the Shadeward manor is a place with specific implications for what things are and who owns them and what they contain. Remi acquired a pillow. Remi did not explain how. The pillow appears in a dance. This is the kind of detail that official historians smooth over and that Waluigi documents exactly because it will not be smoothed over here.

The pillow exists.

It was acquired.

Its origin is unresolved.

WAH.*

It wasn't the best idea, Remi admitted. This is probably the most self-aware thing Remi said on her birthday, and Waluigi finds it significant that she was capable of assessing the pillow-dance ghost-luring strategy as suboptimal in retrospect while having fully committed to it during execution. This is the Remi operational pattern: full commitment to an idea during implementation, honest assessment of the idea afterward. The assessment rarely changes the next idea. But it is honest, and honesty about failure is a form of intelligence that the Shadeward specifically tries to erode, so Waluigi documents it as a positive data point.

Markop and Toad waited in the nearby room. Remi waited alone in the room with the door.

The knock came.

## The Fake Ghost:


The Onyx Knight, the Vampire, and the Contract

Someone knocked and announced themselves as a ghost, in the specific way that nobody announcing themselves as a ghost has ever been a ghost. Remi opened the door.

An Onyx Knight in a blanket sheet, eyes cut. A fake ghost constructed from institutional materials by someone who had heard about Remi's ghost-luring strategy and decided that the strategy created an opportunity. The vampire was with him, or arrived with him, or was already there — the sourcing is imprecise on the sequencing but unanimous on the vampire's presence and objective.

The vampire attempted to coax Remi into following him. Remi believed it was a real ghost. This is a data point about Remi's threat assessment calibration that Waluigi is adding to the running documentation alongside the enthrallment contract near-miss and the conversation with the Beastmaster's intelligence network. Remi assessed the blanket-sheet Onyx Knight as a potentially real ghost. Remi almost signed a document that would have sent her consciousness to a separate dimension. Remi has been documented by the Voss wedding guard as famous for always being tricked. The wedding guard's characterization is cruel.

The documentation is consistent.

Waluigi does not blame Remi for this. Waluigi blames the Shadeward for being an environment specifically engineered to make the real things look fake and the fake things look real. The Shadeward is a dimension that runs on performed reality — imps wear Wario costumes and deliver legally real birth certificates, Onyx Knights wear bedsheets and knock on doors, vampires construct paper standees and announce ambushes from behind them. A person who assumes good faith and takes appearances at face value is not stupid in the Shadeward. They are simply operating with a baseline designed for a different environment.

Remi's baseline was designed for somewhere else.

She has not had enough time in the Shadeward to recalibrate it, and nobody has been consistent enough about teaching her to distrust appearances to produce a usable update.

*Waluigi also wants to note that the vampire's attempt to coax Remi into following him — to ask her to play, to come along — is the same structural move as the enthrallment contract, the teleportation ring, the wedding invitation, and every other attempt the Shadeward's inhabitants have made on Remi since she arrived. They do not seize. They invite. They ask her to come willingly. This is not coincidence. There is something specific about Remi's willing participation that the Shadeward's various factions require, and Waluigi is watching this pattern with the focused attention it deserves. The contract, the ring, the ghost coaxing, the fake Wario with the birth certificate — they all want her to say yes.

They never simply take.

Waluigi does not yet know why.

WAH.*

Sign the contract, the fake ghost said. Remi was presented with a document.

Markop called it out as fake. Because if demons and magic rats and contracts exist, Remi asked, why not ghosts? This is a reasonable epistemological question and a deeply inconvenient one from a tactical standpoint, because Remi was applying the correct framework — in the Shadeward, everything that seems impossible is actually possible — to reach the incorrect conclusion, which is that the thing currently asking her to sign a contract was a real ghost rather than an Onyx Knight in a sheet.

If we throw an arrow at you, will you bleed, Markop asked.

Go ahead and shoot me, the ghost said.

The fake ghost said 'shoot me' because the fake ghost had calculated that nobody would actually shoot him. He was wrong about the threat assessment but right about the immediate outcome, because Remi did not shoot him. Remi prepared to stab him with a dagger instead, because Remi's preferred resolution to ambiguous ghost situations involves edged weapons at close range. The ghost blocked with the contract paper. Markop pulled the sheet from behind.

Onyx Knight. Blanket. Eyes cut out. Standing in a doorway with a vampire and a contract.

The performance had produced a performance. Remi's ghost-luring dance had lured a fake ghost constructed by someone with access to Onyx Knight personnel and a continuing interest in getting Remi's signature on documents. Waluigi wants to flag this because the resources required to stage a fake ghost encounter — briefing an Onyx Knight, coordinating a vampire, producing a contract — are not trivial, and the institutional investment in getting Remi to sign something implies that what she would be signing has significant value to whoever is requesting it.

The Onyx Knight was dragged before the Beastmaster.

## The Beastmaster's Response and the Shadow Crystal Distribution


The Beastmaster was knitting.

Waluigi wants to document this detail specifically because the Beastmaster knitting while someone drags a costumed Onyx Knight before him for wasting the party's time is the most precisely characterful image from the session, and character images matter for understanding the people who inhabit the crisis. The Beastmaster has a Death Lounge full of taxidermied Shadowfell apex predators and named crossbows. He also knits. These facts coexist. The previous entry documented the rugs in his lounge — the Shadow Manes, the Spiny Devourer — and noted that Vaxillus wants to put a ghost's soul in one of his rugs.

The knitting is how the rugs get made.

The Beastmaster is producing the vessels for his collection through an activity associated with domestic patience and craft.

He is making things to put dead things in.

He was doing this when the fake ghost was dragged in.

He gave it a side-eye and kept knitting.

The shadow crystal was distributed. All pieces to the portal except for Remi's share. Markop and Green T agreed on this without making it a formal conversation, which is the agreement style of two people who have independently arrived at the same conclusion and are communicating through the economy of people who do not need to explain themselves to each other because they have been watching the same person make the same kinds of decisions for long enough to share a shorthand.

*They both don't trust Remi with shadow crystal pieces. Waluigi is going to document this directly because it is an important operational fact and because Remi noticed it. She noticed that her share was withheld. She noticed that the decision was made between Markop and Green T without consulting her. The previous session documented that Remi's willingness to share operational objectives with anyone who seems interested has produced a comprehensive intelligence asymmetry favoring the Beastmaster's network. The shadow crystal is a narcotic absorption device with views into future states. The two people with the most operational experience in the party looked at Remi and looked at the shadow crystal and decided that the combination was not one they were willing to produce.

This is correct.

It is also unkind in the specific way that correct decisions about trust are unkind to the person whose trust level is being correctly assessed.

Remi noticed.

Waluigi notices that Remi noticed.

WAH.*

Markop examined the shadow crystal more carefully. It is a shadowy narcotic absorption device — the 'narcotic' characterization is significant and Waluigi is filing it alongside every other piece of intelligence about shadow-adjacent materials in the archive, including the dark fluid from Baldi's wounds and the void-adjacent thermal signature on the object Baldi carries. Narcotic means it affects perception. Narcotic means it changes the user's relationship to reality, not by providing false information but by making the existing information feel different. The crystal also offers permissive views into future states — not prediction, not prophecy, but permission.

The future that the crystal shows is the future as it could be if certain conditions are met, not the future as it must be.

This distinction matters enormously for how the crystal's intelligence is interpreted, and Markop saved it for later, which is the correct decision.

Remi noticed OC and AC on the bottom of the crystal. Orangus Cornelius. Archie — almost certainly Archie Miser, whose documented history with the Shadowfell is extensive and whose presence in Shadeward operations has been woven through the current arc since before the party arrived. The Shadeward arc documentation describes Archie spending approximately a month in the Shadowfell after the anchor event — living in the forest, searching for Green T, being eventually expelled when the manor 'flashed.' A shadow crystal marked AC is a shadow crystal that passed through Archie's hands. The narcotic absorption device that perceives future states was owned by Archie Miser, the man whose magical instability shattered reality into three planes during the planar fracture, whose fire magic was used as the foundation for a synchronization ritual and destabilized it catastrophically, whose capacity for absorbing and channeling power was documented by the Oracle as dangerous enough to require intervention.

*Archie Miser had a shadow crystal that shows futures. Archie Miser absorbed enough magical energy in the Shadowfell to eventually re-ignite his fire magic during the anchor event. Archie Miser then spent a month in the Shadowfell while the Oracle was warning him, back in the material plane, that he was absorbing too much power. The crystal and the month are the same period. Waluigi does not know exactly what Archie was doing with a narcotic future-viewing device during a month of solitary existence in a dimension designed to extinguish hope. Waluigi suspects the crystal's views of future states were part of how Archie maintained operational intent during a period when operational intent should have been impossible to sustain.

You do not stop looking for someone if you can see the futures in which you find them.

WAH.*

## The Gallery: Violet Light, Warded Cases, and the Mirror That Is Not a Painting

The gallery is a room that deserves full documentation because it is one of the most informationally dense spaces the party has entered during the Shadeward arc, and because the party spent most of their time in it either alarming things or jumping out of it rather than reading what it contained.

The gallery is flooded with an uncharacteristically steady violet light from flickering orbs in the far corners. Steady violet light in the Shadeward is unusual — the Shadeward's characteristic illumination is gray and cold and uncertain, light that admits entropy into its wavelength. Violet is specific. Violet is willed. The orbs are maintaining their output against the Shadowfell's ambient drain, which requires either significant magical investment or a connection to a power source that the Shadowfell cannot touch.

The cases are gray wood and leaden glass. All locked. All magically warded. Picking the locks without a key triggers a guard alert and, as the party discovered, a gas response. Kryn and Vivesna carry the keys, which means access to the gallery's contents requires either finding those specific individuals or having something they want badly enough to trade a key for.

Markop's magical detection detected the wards. He noted them. He communicated them. Remi pulled out a picklock.

*Waluigi wants to document the sequence with the precision it deserves. Markop detected the wards. Markop communicated the existence of the wards, which are described as not harmful but unspecified in effect. The detection was shared. The warning was given. Remi then produced a picklock and attempted to open a warded case without a key. This is not a failure of intelligence — Remi received the intelligence. This is a failure of intelligence to translate into behavioral modification, which is a different problem and one that Waluigi has been tracking across multiple Remi incidents during the Raventree operation.

She knows things and does them anyway.

This is not stupidity.

This is the specific operational pattern of someone whose risk assessment is conducted in the moment of action rather than in the planning phase, which means the risk assessment frequently arrives after the action has already produced its consequences.

WAH.*

Waluigi wants to document what was in those cases before documenting the alarm, because the cases' contents are why the party was there and the alarm does not erase their significance.

The Puzzling Case: a jade elephant, a golden knight, and a carved stone king on a throne. The painting — which is not a painting, as will be documented shortly — depicts this case with only the jade elephant present. The other two figures are missing from the reflected version. A clever caster with Locate Object could use the statuettes to find their counterparts in the ruined manor. This implies the statuettes in this case are either originals with counterparts in the ruined manor, or the reflected case is the original state and this case's additional figures represent additions or intruders. The discrepancy is worth tracking.

The Crystal Sword: huge, probably very fragile. A weapon designed to be impressive rather than durable, or a weapon designed for something that swords are not typically designed for.

The Preserved Spiders: one blue, one brown, very large. Waluigi is noting these specifically because preserved specimens in warded cases imply the specimens are either valuable as specimens, valuable as magical components, or dangerous in a state beyond preservation. Large preserved spiders in a Shadowfell gallery are most plausibly dangerous in a state beyond preservation.

The Shadow Log: a single log of dark wood that pulses and twitches with shadowy energy, cut from the woods beyond the estate grounds. The woods beyond the estate grounds are where the Scorncrow operates. Waluigi files this.

The Dark Crystal: two large jagged formations that look like a mixture of obsidian and charcoal and seem to drink in what little light touches them. Shadow-adjacent mineral structures that absorb light. In a room maintained by violet light against the Shadowfell's ambient drain, cases containing light-absorbing crystals are cases that the room's maintenance system is actively fighting against. The orbs and the crystals are in opposition. Someone decided to keep them in the same room.

The Arcane Accretion Set: collectible cards with complex rules and beautiful art. These are the same game as Gonzo Gab from the Feyward Manor — the same game, presented with 'considerably more ostentatiousness,' which is the Shadeward's relationship to the Feyward in miniature. The Feyward has the organic version, growing from fey logic and mushroom-stool card tables. The Shadeward has the formal version, warded in cases, facing down, untouched. Both are card games. The Feyward version is played. The Shadeward version is collected.

The Cloth-Covered Boxes: three small boxes covered in red, blue, and black cloth. Uncovering them produces a brief swirl of ice cold mist and reveals nothing inside. The space is empty and perhaps always was. The cloths, once removed, do not restore the emptiness to containment. Waluigi notes that boxes which contain nothing when examined but maintain their form under covering are either containers for something that only exists when unobserved, or the shrouds themselves are the objects and the boxes are their housing. Either interpretation is consistent with Shadowfell physics.

The Infinity Goblets: five enormous silvery goblets sized for a creature much larger than normal, each affixed with a differently colored jewel. As containers their potential is infinite. Waluigi does not have a current operational need for containers with infinite potential but files them as resources that may become relevant when the artifact acquisition push reaches the phase that requires containing things.

The Diamond and Shield: a giant diamond and a beautifully decorated golden shield. The diamond is large enough to be listed as a notable feature. In the Shadeward, where light is perpetually contested, a giant diamond is a light-storing and light-refracting device of significant magnitude.

The Spider and Mask: an articulated gold spider covered in jewels beside a solid gold mask. The articulation implies movement capacity. An articulated gold spider with jewels, in a warded case, in a Shadowfell gallery — Waluigi is not dismissing this as decorative.

The Metallic Geometric Shapes: a silver pyramid, golden orb, and adamantium cube. Adamantium is the hardest material on the material plane. An adamantium cube in a warded case in a Shadowfell gallery implies the cube's containment is meaningful — you do not ward something you cannot break. The ward is for other reasons.

And then the mirror.

## The Mirror That Is Not a Painting


The large piece on the southeast wall initially appears to be a painting. It depicts what looks like the same gallery in autumn colors, in the light of sunset. Plants growing over everything. Warm orange light.

It is not a painting.

The light dims periodically. Figures move through the depicted space. The space on the other side is the Feyward Manor's version of this same gallery — the same room, in a different plane, overgrown with vines and autumn leaves, the cases showing subtle variations in their contents. This is a planar mirror. A conjuration device. A window between the Shadeward and the Feyward, showing both versions of the same room simultaneously.

Touching it feels warm, like sunlight. In the Shadeward, feeling warmth when you touch a wall is the most profound sensory violation available, because the Shadeward does not contain warmth and the absence of warmth is how the Shadeward reminds you that it is what it is. The mirror contains the warmth of the Feyward through the glass. Waluigi finds this both beautiful and deeply significant as an engineering achievement.

The reflected version of the Puzzling Case shows only the jade elephant. The golden knight and stone king are absent from the Feyward version. They exist in the Shadeward version and not in the Feyward version. This means either they were moved from the Feyward to the Shadeward at some point, or they exist only in the Shadeward as objects without Feyward counterparts, or they are somewhere in the Feyward but not in this specific room. The Locate Object implication from the Puzzling Case description becomes more complex under this reading: if the golden knight and stone king exist only in one plane, their counterparts in the ruined manor may be in the ruined manor's Shadeward version specifically.

The mirror has runes on the back of its frame. Conjuration runes. If the right command phrase or triggering condition is met, it would serve as a doorway. Access to the Feyward from the Shadeward through the gallery mirror. A connection between the two planes that does not require the Midnight Fountain and does not need four artifacts to activate.

Refusing to speak a name is not courtesy.

It is containment.

Vivian C. is not protecting the Oracle's privacy.

She is protecting herself and her correspondent from whatever speaking the name of a ruined Oracle does.

WAH.*

The Corvinarus family — Orangus Cornelius, Vivian C., the broader institutional structure of the Onyx Hand — is opposed to the fake Oracle. They have a plan that requires the party to be thralled and used as instruments. They have the Oracle's apparent agreement. And they have identified, and refuse to name, a ruined Oracle who they consider an opposing force.

Markop said: I knew it. They were trying to trick us.

This is correct. This is also the minimum version of what is true. The full version is that Vivian C. and Kyrn C. have been coordinating a staged operation involving dinner preparations, sent invitations, sleeping-pill-laced food, inner chambers for thralling, a feast on unconscious bodies, a plan to permanently cut the three planes, and the apparent cooperation of the Oracle the party has been treating as an unreliable but genuine guide. And there is a ruined Oracle whose real name Vivian C. will not write, whom she considers fake, and whom the Corvinarus family plan to stop.

Remi found this note in a servant's bathroom in the Shadeward manor on her fourteenth birthday.

She showed it to Markop.

Markop said he knew it.

Green T asked what Remi wanted for her birthday. She said to go home. He stayed silent.

The silence now contains more than it did before the note was found. It contains the knowledge that the planes were being cut. It contains the knowledge that the dinner was staged. It contains the knowledge that the Oracle agreed to something, and that agreement's nature is unresolved. It contains the knowledge that there is a ruined Oracle whose name will not be spoken and who the Corvinarus family considers their primary opposition.

Remi wants to go home. The people planning to cut the three planes are in the same building. The Oracle who agreed to their plan is the party's most consistent navigation point through the entire crisis.

Green T stayed silent.

Waluigi documents everything.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi is documenting Remi's time in the Shadow Estate in full because her arc contains more important intelligence than almost any other character thread in this period, most of it gathered by accident through the simple act of being curious and opening doors.

## The Looting — What Remi Found Before Anyone Was Watching


While the rest of the party was managing dinner politics, fighting undead dancers, and getting dragged through hedge mazes, Remi was systematically searching the Shadow Estate's private spaces.

In Kryn Corvinarus's master bedroom, she found the medicine cabinet: Hemoglue of the Nightlord, Shadowveil Tincture, Stakeheart Salve, Leadfang Extractor, Ebonblood Antidote. She took the Hemoglue and the Extractor — practical choices, trauma-relevant choices, the choices of someone who expected to need wound treatment soon.

Beneath the bedroom rug: an incomplete teleportation circle, etched in chalk and charcoal, approximately one third still glowing with ancient power. Irreparably damaged but alive. Someone had been working on dimensional transit here. Whether Kryn, Vivian, or someone earlier, the circle confirms that multiple parties in the estate were attempting planar movement independent of the Oracle's infrastructure.

In a guest room: Ryan's diary. This is the detail Waluigi finds most significant. Ryan — who jumped from the Vigilance during the Iron Sky Breach — had been in the Shadowfell. His first diary entry documents waking up to grey, watching Archie panic about his fire, calling Bowser's 'candle-man' remark 'typical.' Ryan was present at the Cold Awakening. He then disappeared from the diary before Remi found it, and Remi saw what she believed to be Ryan — static, flickering — through a window before he vanished again.

Remi gathered more useful intelligence before the auction than most operatives gather in a week. None of it was reported in any structured format because Remi is not an intelligence operative. She is just someone who opens doors and remembers what she sees.

## The Vivian Identification — A Wig and Too Much Honesty


Before the petrification, Remi encountered Vivian — operating as Vivesna, the thrall persona — and identified something nobody else had caught.

The hair was fake.

Vivian's hair was a wig — human hair, cut and glued to his actual hair with adhesive. Remi noticed this through casual observation. No magical detection, no investigative protocol. She simply looked and saw what was there.

When Remi confronted Vivian directly, Vivian dropped the pretense entirely — not because he was caught, but because Remi was alone and he had calculated that it no longer mattered.

'I am waiting for both of them to be dead so I can be the new heir,' Vivian said.

Then he told Remi to leave. To let nature take its course.

This conversation happened before the rest of the party knew Vivian was a threat. Remi was the first person to discover the triple identity. She was then immediately separated from the party, which Waluigi suspects was not coincidental — Vivian had just exposed himself and needed her isolated.

## The Entropy Ring — 'Vampire Friends'


Remi received a ring delivered in a letter addressed to her, from 'your vampire friends,' with handwriting she recognized from the estate's guest book.

The ring leaked black smoke. Entropy, the Onyx Hand guards said. It needed recharging, they said.

Markop's ritual examination later confirmed the ring carried destructive necrotic magic. The 'friendship ring' framing was cover for what was functionally a tracking and influence artifact. Someone who had been watching Remi since the guest book — since before dinner, possibly since before the party arrived — had sent her a magical device disguised as sentiment.

Who wrote in the guest book? Waluigi does not know. The handwriting connects the ring to whoever registered the party's presence. The entropy leakage connects it to the Iron Legion's ring technology. These two facts together suggest someone with access to both the estate's social protocols and Legion magical infrastructure.

The ring was later 'recharged' by the Onyx Hand guards, producing more black smoke. Whether this recharging represented maintenance of a beneficial enchantment or escalation of a control mechanism, Remi cannot determine and the guards were not forthcoming.

## The Petrification — Lyranth's Workshop


Remi was funneled to the workshop. Every door had guards except one. The Archivist had separated her from her friends using the transformed imps. Bowser had retreated to protect the remaining party. One door remained open.

The workshop contained Lyranth — the medusa artist who creates sculptures from the bodies of those who meet her gaze. Her tools were sculptor's tools. Her sculptures were people. The craft was genuine; the material was not quarried stone.

Lyranth looked at Remi. Said 'smile.' Remi turned to stone.

The word 'smile' is artistic direction. Lyranth wants her subjects to have pleasant expressions when they become permanent. This detail — a medusa who asks for a smile before she petrifies you — is either the most grotesque thing in the Shadow Estate or the most honest thing in the Shadow Estate, depending on how you look at it. She is at least transparent about what she is doing and what she wants from it.

Remi, frozen mid-expression, became the third statue in the workshop.

## The Auction — Art Display 'feat. Archie Miser'


The Archivist had distributed a poster before the auction even began: 'Official Art Display feat. Archie Miser' with an image of Remi as stone.

Waluigi has written about the Archivist's one-way mirror revelation elsewhere — the window swung open, the Archivist informed Eager that vampires do not appear in mirrors, Eager fell to the ground. But the poster detail deserves emphasis. The Archivist named the exhibition after Archie, who was not present, had not consented, and had nothing to do with Remi's petrification. The naming was deliberate institutional branding — attaching Archie's name to Remi's suffering as a way of advertising the event to those who would find Archie's association interesting.

This tells Waluigi that the Archivist is deeply embedded in whatever faction-level intelligence surrounds Archie. He knew Archie's name was worth marketing. He knew attaching it to a stone toad would draw an audience. The Archivist is not merely a vampire librarian. He is an information operator using institutional position to shape events.

The auction was won by Purple T for twelve thousand gold. The rest of the brawl is documented in the auction entries Waluigi has already filed.
